title: Muscles of the anterior and lateral leg (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Lateral condyle and upper half of the lateral surface of the tibia, and the interosseous membrane.
Medial cuneiform and the base of the first metatarsal.
Dorsiflexes the foot at the ankle and inverts the foot.
hy: When the deep fibular or common fibular nerve is injured the foot cannot be dorsiflexed (foot drop), and the person lifts the knee high to clear the toes (steppage gait).

rows: Lateral condyle of the tibia, the upper three-quarters of the medial surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
Middle and distal phalanges of the lateral four toes.
Extends the lateral four toes and dorsiflexes the foot.
Middle part of the medial surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe.
Extends the great toe and dorsiflexes the foot.
hy: Weak extension of the great toe is the classic test for the L5 nerve root, as with a herniated disc between L4 and L5.

rows: Lower third of the medial surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
Dorsal surface of the base of the fifth metatarsal.
Dorsiflexes the foot and helps evert it.
Head and upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
Base of the first metatarsal and the medial cuneiform. Its tendon passes behind the lateral malleolus and crosses the sole in the groove of the cuboid.
Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes it. Supports the transverse arch of the foot.
Lower two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
Tuberosity on the base of the fifth metatarsal.
Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes it.
hy: In a forced inversion of the foot its pull can tear the tuberosity off the base of the fifth metatarsal (avulsion fracture).

rows: Upper surface of the front part of the calcaneus.
Joins the tendons of extensor digitorum longus to the second, third and fourth toes.
Helps extend the second, third and fourth toes.
Upper surface of the front part of the calcaneus, with extensor digitorum brevis.
Base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe.
